newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S FARMING MINISTER SAYS WILL RESIGN.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S FARMING MINISTER SAYS WILL RESIGN.

text.p: Poland's Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski, pressured by the leadership of his Polish Peasant Party (PSL) to quit, said on Saturday he would step down to avoid an open rift in his party.

"I have expressed my will to hand in my resignation," Jagielinski told private Radio Zet after the meeting of his party's Supreme Council which was to decide his fate after PSL's executive body last month demanded his resignation.

PSL chief Waldemar Pawlak and a group of Peasant leaders accused Jagielinski, who is also a deputy prime minister, of pursuing farm policies that ill served farmers' interests and brought a $1 billion deficit in food trade last year.
"For the good of PSL and Polish countryside I am doing this (resigning). One should not hold on to a post in a situation when it divides the Polish Peasant Party," Jagielinski added.
He said he had yet to decide when he would submit the resignation.

Up to now Jagielinski had resisted the pressure defending government policies and had said it was up to Prime Minister Wlodzmierz Cimoszewicz to decide whether he should go and Cimoszewicz has defended Jagielinski's record.

Jagielinski's departure would avert an open rift in PSL between his liberal-minded supporters and a group of leaders representing interests of hosts of small farmers wary of reforms and strongly lobbying for government subsidies.
Analysts have said the dismissal of Jagielinski, a succesfull large landowner, might boost PSL's rating in rural areas, where small, often poor farmers dominate.

The decision should also allow the three-year often uneasy coalition of the Peasants with the bigger ex-communist SLD, get back to business after PSL leaders refused to cooperate with SLD as long as Jagielinski stayed in office.
